speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: He said this in his supplementary question after my reply on sporting privileges for National Servicemen.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF had provided all relevant facts of NS liabilities for new citizens in a written answer to his Parliamentary Question that he had filed for that same Sitting in July.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They number on average 3,400 each year, which constitute about half of all new male citizens registered each year." In fact, we had prepared this same reply in May, because Mr Leong had filed a similar question then, but which he withdrew when there was no Sitting that month.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Even before the July Sitting, Mr Leong had been repeating these misleading statements in two Facebook posts: one in late May and another on 1 July.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In late May, I quote: "Is it fair for foreigners to be given citizenship without doing NS while our locally-born Singaporeans have to serve NS despite having valid reasons to defer?" For his Facebook post in July, I quote: "Is it fair that we forfeit our local talents their chances of developing their talents while many new male citizens do not need to do NS?" Let there be no doubt that for every young male citizen, whether by birth, registration or descent, the NS liabilities are the same.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They will be enlisted for NS at 18 years or older to perform full-time NS, and thereafter must fulfil their Operationally Ready NS (ORNS) duties.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But if a foreigner comes to Singapore and becomes a citizen as a mature adult, typically in his 30s or 40s, we exempt him from NS because he did not enjoy any socioeconomic benefits like young Singaporeans and also because he would be too old to enlist for full time NS.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: On a topic as important as NS, Mr Leong should have waited for MINDEF's reply or sought the full facts.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This policy is not new; in fact, it dates back at least to the early 1980s.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We had to go some way back to find out when the policy started.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But it is, at least, more than 40 years.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is in our Parliamentary records as Ministers and Members of Parliament have spoken on this policy previously.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For example, back in 2007, then-Minister of State for Defence Assoc Prof Koo Tsai Kee had already made clear that: "Each year, we have a number of new citizens in full-time NS.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: They are born foreign nationals, they took up permanent residency, but have since been naturalised as Singapore Citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Like those who are born Singaporeans, they are enlisted for full-time NS upon reaching enlistment age and contribute to Operationally Ready NS thereafter." It is also easy to get the relevant information on the Internet.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: If you key in in your search engine: "NS, new citizens, Singapore", it pops up.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Many fora make it known that new young male citizens must do NS and that those who become citizens as mature adults are exempted.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, this policy is well publicised on the Internet too.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This long-standing policy has served our defence needs.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Over the years, Permanent Residents (PRs) and young male new citizens have formed an increasing proportion of NS enlistees.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In other words, PRs and young male new citizens formed 5% in the early 2000s.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: So, what Mr Leong asserts is not true.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Many new citizens are enlisted for NS every year.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: New citizens and PRs are contributing to our national defence.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: And without that extra inject of new citizens and PRs, our smaller birth cohorts would have impacted SAF's manpower needs more acutely.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: I have decided that it is important to correct the misleading statements put out by Mr Leong, because they strike at the foundations of equity and universality that underpin National Service in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Just think about it – if pre-enlistees are misled into thinking that new citizens of their age are exempted, where will they have the heart to serve NS?

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The correct facts must be put out to reassure the National Servicemen in the SAF and Home Team.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: National Service is the bedrock of the SAF and our national defence.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Members of Parliament have the duty to ask questions and debate policies, including NS policies, in this House.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But they should not make misleading statements that can weaken NS, the SAF and Home Team.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, before you ask your clarifications, can I just remind you that it is for clarifications, no speeches, please.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister has spent the last 15 to 20 minutes talking about what I have written, what I have said, and has pointed some accusations at me.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I think I am entitled to a full speech.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: You can register your objection but no speeches, as per Standing Order No 23.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: First of all, I thank the Minister for responding today to my recent Parliamentary Questions and also for pointing out some of the views I have expressed.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I think this really is good because it makes a robust response and debate in this House.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: My Parliamentary Questions are actually prompted by the Ukraine war and the passionate speech made by the Foreign Affairs Minister Dr Vivian Balakrishnan —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: In that case, I would like to ask the fundamental question.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The fundamental question is, yes, the Minister has provided data on some of the PRs and the new citizens who have contributed to our National Service in recent years.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: However, I think there are still a significant number of new citizens who did not —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: So, just based on some of the Parliamentary Questions I have filed recently, I make an estimate that over the last 21 years —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I am going to ask you to please ask your questions and not make statements.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Otherwise, I would have to ask you to —

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Okay, then I ask the Minister: what is the number of new citizens who did not do NS?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: You still have to give me that number.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It does not mean that 10% of our annual enlistment now consists of new citizens, then all the new citizens have performed NS, right?

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We have a full display of Mr Leong's modus operandi.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: We started at 3.00 pm and even with this speech, it is now 3.11 pm.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: He says I did not give him the facts.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: In fact, when I replied to his question in this Parliamentary Question – why for sportsmen, we have to be very selective in their deferment – my principal argument was equity and universality.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: He ignored all of it and he jumped in, and now, he says, "Well, I wasn't really referring to the young ones.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I was just referring to others who were exempted." But he did not give the facts.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: He has not denied that he knew all the facts.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: He has not defended whether he knew, or he spoke out differently.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: He has just said, well, he has got other questions.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I am going to allow you just one last clarification so that we can move on.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Yes, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I think the Minister opened up the debate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I got a number here just provided by MHA —

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, since you have asked for the facts, let the Minister repeat it first, and then, you can clarify.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: I will repeat what we have given him, the reply to him and the exact information he has asked.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, you can take a seat for now.

speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
text: The information is both in the written reply and today's session.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, the Minister has given the facts.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The number the Minister has given only forms a subset of the new citizens.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: It does not form the whole new citizens' number.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Okay, Mr Leong, you have asked your clarification.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Minister, would you like to reply to that?

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Leong, I am going to advise you.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: He has repeated it several times in his speech.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: I would ask you to look at that again.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: If you still have further clarifications, then I would advise you to file a Parliamentary Question for the next Sitting.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: I have an estimate, but I am waiting for the Minister to give me more numbers.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: But anyway, I accept that and I will file a Parliamentary Question.
